# Azure Arc onboarding role: a pinned copy of Microsoft's Ansible role

This folder is an unmodified copy of the `azure_arc` role from the `azure.azcollection` Ansible collection, the role Microsoft Learn documents in [Connect machines to Azure Arc at scale with Ansible](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-arc/servers/onboard-ansible-playbooks). It comes from [ansible-collections/azure](https://github.com/ansible-collections/azure/tree/afa62c3bcf3e283645336039e13c8e3019b8fcdd/roles/azure_arc) at commit `afa62c3bcf3e283645336039e13c8e3019b8fcdd`, the `v4.2.0` release of October 30, 2026; the role's files last changed on August 13, 2026. `LICENSE` is the repository's license, GPL-3.0-or-later, as the role's `meta/main.yml` states. The collection's Galaxy manifest says GPL-2.0-or-later; the repository's license file is the one copied here.

**What's here, and why.** The role's README, defaults, metadata and tasks: everything `examples/ansible/playbooks/06_arc_onboarding_role.yml` runs when it calls `azure.azcollection.azure_arc`. The playbook runs the role from the installed collection, pinned to 4.2.0 in `examples/ansible/requirements.yml`, not from this folder; the copy is here so the role can be read and reviewed in the repository, and so `examples/ansible/tests/test_microsoft_role.py` can pin what the role does and leaves out. The same test fails if the installed role differs from this copy. The collection's modules aren't copied; `snapshot.json` lists what was left out. The [developer workbook *Building the Attribute-Driven Migration*, Chapter 08](../../../docs/books/b19-developer-workbook/08-ansible-beside-arc.md) explains the gaps.

**How it stays honest.**

- `snapshot.json` records the upstream repository, path, commit, dates, license and the size and SHA-256 of every file here. Each file's git blob hash was checked against the upstream tree at the commit before the manifest was written, and the role files in the 4.2.0 Galaxy release were checked against these hashes. `scripts/tests/test_third_party_snapshots.py` fails if any file is changed, added or removed.
- The weekly source watch follows commits to the upstream folder (`azure-arc-role-commits` in `data/source-watch/feeds.json`) and reports each one in its issue under DW (developer workbooks).
- To move to a newer release: review the upstream change, copy the role from that release's commit, regenerate `snapshot.json`, move the pin in `examples/ansible/requirements.yml`, rerun `examples/ansible/tests/test_microsoft_role.py` and the Chapter 08 labs, and open a pull request. Never edit the files here; changes the program needs go in `examples/ansible`.

These files keep their upstream bytes, line endings included, so the hashes match the upstream commit.
